messages:
Morgan: quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak (now preferring fused-kv kernels for several Llama2 variants) we're seeing 95p latency regressions for short-seq tenants on prod-dedicated. :confused:
Anil: can you paste the perf numbers? short-seq meaning <32 tokens?
Morgan: yeah <32 tokens. baseline 95p was ~40ms, now ~110-140ms for some small tenants. throughput for long seqs looks fine.
Tara: that smells like batching/queue formation change — fused-kv kernel increases per-item latency for mini-batches? or we're coalescing long+short too aggressively.
Jack: agree. I want to see KV hit profile. If short sequences miss KV and cause long warmups, they can clog the micro-batcher.
Morgan: attaching quick profile snippet from a canary window: ```
# profile summary
window: 2026-03-12T22:00Z
tenant: short-ssd-prod
avg_batch_size: 18
median_seq_len: 12
kv_hit_rate: 0.28
95p_latency: 128ms
dominant_kernel: fused_kv_v3
```
Priya: 0.28 kv hit is low for short tenants; maybe fused-kv introduces larger per-token setup cost for small KV caches. Also kernel selection may be picking fused-kv because of model tag heuristics (embedding of kv-enabled flag).
Anil: hypothesis: the kernel selector heuristic uses expected seq length distribution aggregated per model, not per-request. After the change, mixed queues fill with a lot of long requests and the batcher waits to hit cost-optimal size — short requests wait and get starved.
Tara: can we get queue traces? I'm curious about queue wait time distribution broken out by seq length buckets.
Morgan: grabbed traces for the last 3 hours, short-seq queue-wait 90p=75ms, long-seq queue-wait 90p=18ms. So short ones are waiting more.
Jack: ouch. That indicates scheduling bias. Two knobs to consider: (1) lane-based token budgets (reserve small burst credits for short lane) (2) fast-path preemption / short-lane bypass that ejects part of the batch if a short has waited > X ms.
Priya: also consider kernel fallback: if fused-kv kernel has worse p95 for batch_size < N, prefer small-kernel for batches dominated by short seqs. We already collect perf matrix per (kernel, batch_size, seq_len). Might be time to use it in selector.
Anil: propose a quick experiment: create a short-lane with token_budget_target=0.6 (higher refill) and max_wait_ms=10, and route 10% of short-tenant traffic over it. If p95 improves without hurting long tenants, we expand.
Tara: +1. Also add an A/B for kernel routing: for that 10% route, force kernel=small-kernel-v2. Compare kv_hit rates and end-to-end p95.
Morgan: command I used locally to simulate routing: ```
# simulate short-lane routing canary
rbctl route set --lane short-lane-canary --kernel small-kernel-v2 --token-budget 0.6 --max-wait-ms 10 --pct 10
```
Jack: add dashboards: 1) p95 by tenant-length-bucket, 2) queue-wait histogram per lane, 3) kernel-selection counts per model-version. Need these up before canary.
eng-bot: deploy to canary cluster scheduled 2026-03-13T01:00Z (job id: deploy-7612) :rocket:
Priya: one more thought — KV cache eviction policy might be biased by lane mixing. If long seqs warm the cache with deep KV, short tenants miss and then suffer first-request cost. Consider soft-isolation: keep a tiny per-tenant/bucket sticky segment or prefer local cache allocations for short-lane.
Anil: good point. For canary let's keep kv config unchanged but collect per-tenant kv-warmup traces. If warmup rate drops on short-lane with small-kernel, it's a win.
Morgan: plan summary: (a) add short-lane canary 10% with token_budget=0.6, max_wait=10ms, kernel override small-kernel-v2 (b) add dashboards and queue traces (c) collect kv-warmup & p95 for 24h then decide expand.
Tara: timeline?
Morgan: deploy scheduled by eng-bot at 01:00Z, collect 24h, quick sync tomorrow 11am PT.
Jack: if canary shows improvement, followups: implement selector that uses batch-size x seq-dist perf matrix + per-lane token soft-reservations. Also explore micro-batcher preemption where we flush partial batch if short requests hit wait threshold.
Priya: noted — I'll draft a short RFC for the selector change and micro-batcher preemption after we see canary results.
Anil: sounds good. Thanks Morgan for the spike. :thumbsup:
Morgan: thanks team. will paste links to the dashboards once they exist.
